items.title: Antonelli leads disrupted FP2 as Gasly explains his high-speed spin
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set 1:23.077 to lead George Russell by 0.127s, with Norris and Piastri third and fourth. Two red flags—gravel and Pierre Gasly’s spin—extended FP2 by 13 minutes and left many drivers without an uninterrupted soft-tyre run. Gasly said the earlier stoppage left his tyres below temperature and pressure, increasing bottoming; Alpine management also pointed to the car’s handling difficulties.
items.why_it_matters: The classification is official, but the red flags interrupted run plans. Gasly’s explanation is his account, and Alpine cited the car’s handling too; do not treat the incident as settled driver error or a single confirmed cause.

items.title: Hamilton reports a loss of power as Ferrari repairs Leclerc’s floor
items.summary: Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari floor was repaired after his FP2 spin through the gravel. Later, Lewis Hamilton stopped off track after reporting “I’ve lost power”, prompting a Virtual Safety Car. The official session report does not establish a cause for Hamilton’s loss of power.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the power-loss cause unconfirmed until a team or official report identifies it; do not turn a driver radio message into a diagnosed power-unit failure.

items.title: Norris expects a fight for P3 as Friday analysis puts Mercedes ahead
items.summary: Norris said Friday that McLaren could be fighting for P3 and estimated Mercedes were 0.6–0.7 seconds per lap ahead; he said the team planned to run its newer floor Saturday. Verstappen described Red Bull’s balance as disconnected and understeering. The Race’s traffic-adjusted FP2 long-run analysis estimated Antonelli 0.810 seconds per lap quicker than Verstappen and noted Ferrari did not complete a representative long run.
items.why_it_matters: These are attributed Friday assessments, not a qualifying prediction. The 0.810-second comparison is The Race’s traffic-adjusted analysis, not an official classification; the Practice 3 results page currently has no classification.

items.title: Tyre wear prompts another review; official allocation sources still conflict
items.summary: The Race reported localized 100% wear indicators on the most-abused front-left tyres after 15 laps of high-fuel running. PlanetF1 reports no immediate pressure or 27-lap-limit change after Friday’s review, with another evaluation after Saturday; no matching official Pirelli statement or revised FIA prescription appears in the current sources checked. Formula1.com’s 10:05 UTC preview lists 2 C1 / 3 C2 / 8 C3 plus a separate Q3 Soft, while its 10:43 UTC explainer lists 2 / 4 / 7. Pirelli’s official release and FIA Document 13 V2 confirm C1/C2/C3 and the 27-lap cap, not the per-driver totals.
items.why_it_matters: Attribute the reported no-change decision to PlanetF1 pending official confirmation, and keep the allocation discrepancy unresolved. Do not infer remaining sets or record a post-qualifying race strategy before the official chart is available and reviewed.
